subject.title: Gateway boot: no observability for subsystem startup failures (gmail-watcher, hooks)

question: What fixed-vocabulary Gateway boot-summary contract should OpenClaw expose for startup sidecars and hooks, including Gmail watcher skipped reasons and redaction rules?
rationale: The source gap is clear, but subsystem scope, reason wording, and scheduled-versus-started semantics are user-visible operator contracts that automation should not define alone.

options.title: Approve narrow fixed-vocabulary summary
options.body: Add one redacted startup outcome line for Gateway-owned sidecars and hooks, including Gmail watcher skipped reasons, with tests proving no raw secrets or paths are logged.

options.title: Limit this to Gmail watcher diagnostics
options.body: Only surface Gmail watcher skipped reasons now and defer broader subsystem boot summary work to a later diagnostics design.

options.title: Defer to diagnostics surfaces
options.body: Keep normal startup logs compact and require operators to use health, readiness, status, or diagnostics export for subsystem startup state.

recommendation.title: Approve narrow fixed-vocabulary summary
recommendation.body: Add one redacted startup outcome line for Gateway-owned sidecars and hooks, including Gmail watcher skipped reasons, with tests proving no raw secrets or paths are logged.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete has strong history across the Gmail lifecycle and Gateway startup logging surfaces that define this operator-facing contract.
